strategy_title: Broken Autotune Grid Causes Catastrophic Instruction Explosion
strategy_description: When @triton.autotune is added but the grid lambda is NOT updated to use META['XBLOCK'] (grid remains hardcoded to cdiv(xnumel, 1)), the kernel is launched with 2048 blocks regardless of the autotuned XBLOCK value. Each block then redundantly processes the same output rows, causing executed instructions to balloon from ~520M to ~21B (40x increase) and duration to increase from 807 µs to 155 ms (192x regression). The fix requires the grid to be a lambda: `lambda META: (triton.cdiv(xnumel, META['XBLOCK']),)` so block count scales inversely with XBLOCK. Additionally, when autotune injects XBLOCK automatically, passing XBLOCK as an explicit kwarg in the kernel call causes a conflict; the explicit kwarg must be removed, but the grid must also be updated simultaneously.
applicable_when: Any Triton kernel where @triton.autotune is added to vary XBLOCK (or any tiling parameter that affects grid size). The grid must always be a lambda consuming META to reflect the autotuned tile size.
do_not_apply_when: Never use a static/hardcoded grid when @triton.autotune varies a parameter that determines the number of blocks. This pattern always causes catastrophic regression: blocks multiply redundantly, instruction count explodes proportionally to (autotuned_XBLOCK / original_XBLOCK).
framework_notes: Triton-specific: @triton.autotune injects constexpr config values (XBLOCK, R0_BLOCK, etc.) into the kernel automatically. The grid callable receives META dict with these values. If the grid is a static tuple computed before autotune runs, it will always use the pre-autotune tile size, causing over-subscription and redundant work. Always pair autotune with a lambda grid: `grid = lambda META: (triton.cdiv(N, META['XBLOCK']),)`.
